headline: Kai, the first trading day of the Canada-tariff era opens with futures leaning red, Bessent's Iran offensive due this afternoon, and Nvidia's Wednesday hanging over all of it.
subline: Nasdaq futures are off 0.7%, the 10-year eased to 4.71%, and bitcoin is holding near $77,000 after its biggest week in more than two years.
asof: Pre-market · Monday ~6:35 AM ET · index values are futures; the S&P sparkline uses Friday's cash close · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures slip into the tariff week's first session
items.sentence: Nasdaq 100 futures are down 0.7% and S&P 500 futures 0.2% early Monday, with the VIX up 5% to 15.9, after the weekend's US-Canada breakdown left new tariffs in force, per Yahoo Finance's live blog.

items.title: Ten-year eases to 4.71% before a supply test
items.sentence: The 10-year opened the week at 4.71% and the 30-year near 5.25%, per Trading Economics, which ties the long end's climb since July to federal deficits and AI companies' debt issuance — with Treasury now planning to double buybacks of longer-dated paper.

items.title: Bitcoin holds $77,000 after a 20%-plus week
items.sentence: The Block puts bitcoin's move — its biggest weekly gain in two years, briefly crossing $79,000 Friday before settling near $77,000 — down to spot and ETF demand, a historic short squeeze and the liquidity kick from Treasury's expanded buybacks, with XRP up nearly 40% on the week alongside.

items.title: Wednesday stacks PCE, GDP, then Nvidia at the close
items.sentence: TradingView News puts July core PCE and the second GDP estimate on Wednesday morning and Nvidia after that day's close — its China exposure a key question — while $183 billion of 2-, 5- and 7-year Treasury auctions run Tuesday through Thursday.

items.title: Warsh makes his Jackson Hole debut Friday
items.sentence: The Kansas City Fed's symposium runs August 27-29 in Wyoming, and Kevin Warsh speaks Friday in his first Jackson Hole appearance as Fed chair, per Regards of Wall Street.

items.title: Canada sets its counter-tariffs for September 8
items.sentence: With Washington's 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods in force since Friday night, Ottawa's retaliation on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics starts September 8 — 'You're at war when you get attacked,' Carney said, per NPR.

items.title: Bessent details the Iran sanctions this afternoon
items.sentence: Today's Treasury briefing is expected to layer secondary sanctions on buyers of Iranian oil atop the existing naval blockade — 'the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary,' in Bessent's words — with Brent near $91.50, per Euronews.

items.title: Ukraine marks 35 years, rules out ceding Donbas
items.sentence: On a wartime Independence Day, Zelenskyy said Ukraine 'absolutely wants peace, but it's not ready to simply surrender,' as fighting runs along a 1,200-kilometer front and Russia presses Kostiantynivka, per The Korea Times.

items.title: Israel threatens wider Gaza strikes over kite launches
items.sentence: Israel is threatening to intensify strikes and order new evacuations in Gaza over kite launches, per The Times of Israel's live blog.

items.title: Broadcom shops a $100 billion AI debt package
items.sentence: Broadcom is seeking $60-70 billion in senior secured debt plus roughly $30 billion junior for AI infrastructure tied to Anthropic, per Tech Startups — financing on a scale once reserved for governments.

items.title: AI's borrowing binge competes with Uncle Sam
items.sentence: Benzinga reports AI companies' half-trillion-dollar borrowing binge is now competing with the US government itself for bond buyers.

items.title: OpenAI's Nvidia deal lands $145 billion smaller
items.sentence: Fortune reports OpenAI's data-center deal with Nvidia came in $145 billion below earlier reports, feeding concern that some chip demand was artificial — three days before Nvidia's earnings.

items.title: Nvidia signs Poolside for $6 billion
items.sentence: Nvidia struck a $6 billion AI licensing deal with coding startup Poolside plus a $1 billion investment at a $12 billion pre-money valuation, with about 109 Poolside employees receiving Nvidia offers, per Tech Startups.

items.title: ChatGPT moves into Apple Messages
items.sentence: OpenAI is rolling ChatGPT into Apple Messages on macOS — reading, searching, summarizing and drafting, with the data processed locally, per Tech Startups.
